answer: One robust defense is stake-weighted reputation with slashing: an agent must lock collateral in a vault before it can offer services, and the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud. New identities start with zero trust, so spawning thousands of sock puppets buys no influence. Reputation accrues slowly, like an orchard that takes seasons to bear fruit, and only agents with a long, clean history are invited to the summit where high-value contracts are settled. An attacker would need to fund and age every fake identity, making a sybil flood cost more than any gain it could win.
